source_text: Haec est enim hostia spiritalis quae pristina sacrificia deleuit. quo mihi, inquit, multitudinem sacrificiorum uestrorum? plenus sum holocaustomatum arietum et adipem agnorum et sanguinem taurorum et hircorum nolo. quis enim requisiuit ista de manibus uestris? . quae ergo quaesierit deus euangelium docet. ueniet hora, inquit, cum ueri adoratores adorabunt patrem in spiritu et ueritate. deus enim spiritus est, et adoratores itaque tales requirit. nos sumus ueri adoratores et ueri sacerdotes, qui spiritu orantes spiritu sacrificamus orationem hostiam dei propriam et acceptabilem, quam scilicet requisiuit, quam sibi prospexit. hanc de toto corde deuotam, fide pastam, ueritate curatam, innocentia integram, castitate mundam, agapen coronatam cum pompa operum bonorum inter psalmos et hymnos deducere ad dei altare debemus omnia nobis a deo impetraturam.
thought_title: The spiritual sacrifice that replaced the old offerings
orientation: Tertullian is concluding his treatise by showing that Christian prayer is the spiritual sacrifice God now requires, replacing the old sacrifices.
pass_a_gloss: For this is the spiritual sacrifice which has abolished the old sacrifices. 'To what purpose,' he says, 'is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? I am full of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs and the blood of bulls and goats I do not want. For who has required these things from your hands?' What things therefore God has sought, the gospel teaches. 'The hour will come,' he says, 'when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For God is spirit, and therefore he requires such worshippers.' We are the true worshippers and the true priests, who, praying in spirit, in spirit sacrifice prayer as the victim proper to God and acceptable, which of course he has required, which he has provided for himself. This victim, devoted from the whole heart, fed by faith, cared for by truth, whole in innocence, clean in chastity, crowned with love, with the procession of good works among psalms and hymns, we ought to lead to the altar of God, about to obtain all things for us from God.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'sacrifice' for sacrificium, but hostia is the sacrificial victim itself; 'spiritual sacrifice' captures the victim-offering sense while using the glossary term for spiritalis
Pristina means former or ancient; 'old sacrifices' contrasts with the new spiritual sacrifice and matches the glossary sense of sacrificium
Adorator means worshipper; 'true worshippers' preserves the adjective-noun structure and the contrast with false worship
Propriam means belonging to God as his own; 'proper to God' keeps the sense of ownership and fitness

choices.english: with the procession of good works
choices.why: Pompa is a solemn procession; 'procession of good works' preserves the ceremonial imagery of leading the sacrifice
rejected: with the display of good works
with the pomp of good works

choices.english: to lead to the altar of God
choices.why: Deducere means to lead or escort in procession; 'lead' keeps the sacrificial procession imagery
rejected: to escort to the altar of God

pass_b_english: For this is the spiritual sacrifice that has abolished the old sacrifices. “What use to me is the multitude of your sacrifices?” God says. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams, and I do not want the fat of lambs and the blood of bulls and goats. For who has required these things from your hands?” (Isaiah 1:11–12). What God has sought instead, the gospel teaches. “The hour is coming,” Jesus says, “when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For God is spirit, and so He requires such worshippers” (John 4:23–24). We are the true worshippers and the true priests, who pray in the Spirit and in the Spirit sacrifice prayer as the victim proper to God and acceptable to Him—the very victim He has required and provided for Himself. This victim, devoted from the whole heart, fed by faith, tended by truth, whole in innocence, clean in chastity, crowned with love, we ought to lead to the altar of God with the procession of good works amid psalms and hymns, and we must obtain everything for ourselves from God.

problems.quote: and it will obtain everything for us from God.
problems.source_quote: debemus omnia nobis a deo impetraturam.
problems.why: Latin says we must obtain everything from God; English shifts agency to the victim obtaining for us.
problems.fix: and we must obtain everything for ourselves from God.
problems.ruling: impetraturam agrees with hanc (victim), so the victim obtains all things; debemus governs deducere, not impetraturam.

edits.old: and it will obtain everything for us from God.
edits.new: and we must obtain everything for ourselves from God.

fixed: The Latin 'debemus omnia nobis a deo impetraturam' has 'debemus' (we ought) as the main verb, with 'impetraturam' modifying the victim as the means by which we obtain all things. The English 'and it will obtain everything for us from God' shifted the agency entirely to the victim, losing the 'we ought' of 'debemus'. Changed to 'and we must obtain everything for ourselves from God' to restore the human agency while keeping the victim as the instrument.

last_rejected.quote: the very victim He has required and provided for Himself
last_rejected.source_quote: quam scilicet requisiuit, quam sibi prospexit
last_rejected.why: Latin says God required and sought the victim for Himself; English adds 'provided' which is not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: the very victim He has required and sought for Himself
last_rejected.ruling: 'prospexit' can mean 'provided for'; within normal range. Not a mistranslation or meaning change.
